scope_note: Unresolved implementation dependencies and optional directions after making SQL a required clean-replay participant. Statuses are current to this stage; proposed checks are not executed.

leads.title: First DuckDB v1.0.x point release containing the #12596 fix
leads.detail: Exact source at v1.0.0 lacks the guard; exact source at v1.1.0 has the guard and regression-test file [S24-S26]. v1.0.1/1.0.2 or other point tags were not checked. The tagged test was not executed.
leads.next_step: Inspect the relevant v1.0.x release tags/source and run test_12596.test against supported release binaries; state source and binary conclusions separately.

leads.title: Exact supported DuckDB package/build and Python matrix
leads.detail: The selected design requires Python and SQL nodes to load the same pinned DuckDB Python package/build, but the current docs capture is moving and no exact production wheel/version was selected or run. The example build strings in W5 are placeholders.
leads.next_step: Choose one exact DuckDB patch per supported platform, lock wheel hashes/extensions/config, test Python 3.11-3.13 compatibility, and run the mixed-node replay validation V8.

leads.title: Actual mixed Python notebook and SQL node replay
leads.detail: W5 checks only a candidate-authored fingerprint/invalidation model; it hashes SQL source but does not execute SQL or DuckDB. The graph scheduler, named artifact hand-off, result materialization, progress/cancel, and shared event format are design choices without an implementation check.
leads.next_step: Implement a tiny actual DuckDB SQL node and fresh Python notebook replay consuming its Parquet output; compare two complete event/output manifests and SQL-only invalidation.

leads.title: 5 GB operation envelope and spill behavior
leads.detail: Buffer-pool eviction and file readers are source evidence, not measured performance. Sort, distinct, join, aggregate spill limits and disk use are unknown for 8 cores/16 GB.
leads.next_step: Run proposed validation V11 on generated CSV, NDJSON, and Parquet inputs; record peak RSS, temp disk, latency, and cancellation behavior by operation class.

leads.title: Production OS execution isolation and platform coverage
leads.detail: The proposal needs process isolation, filesystem/network restrictions, and resource limits. No production OS primitive, Windows/macOS behavior, or escape test is established by the candidate check.
leads.next_step: Select a supported OS boundary, run filesystem/network/resource escape and kill tests, and define the unsupported-platform fallback before shipping.

leads.title: Portable artifact serialization and deterministic row identity
leads.detail: Parquet bytes, schema metadata, floating-point representation, format-aware logical record ordinals, and hash stability across platform/build are not proven. An unordered SQL result has no implied stable order.
leads.next_step: Specify typed canonical hashing and stable row-ID rules; test duplicate rows, null/missing distinctions, sort ties, schema evolution, and cross-platform output comparison.

leads.title: Format-specific schema and missing/null contract
leads.detail: The current proposal requires presence information where absent JSON fields must differ from explicit null, but no real DuckDB conversion path was run for heterogeneous NDJSON, timestamps, or evolving schemas.
leads.next_step: Use tiny CSV/NDJSON/Parquet fixtures to pin import/conversion rules and verify reject-ledger behavior across projection and schema changes.

leads.title: marimo issue and runtime status if reconsidering its runtime
leads.detail: Supplied search capture reports #9881 and #10602 open and #10915 unmerged as of 2026-10-05, while #10912 is merged [S21]. The design does not adopt marimo runtime, and current states/fixes were not refreshed.
leads.next_step: Recheck exact issue/PR bodies and released behavior only if marimo becomes a selected component.

leads.title: Project locking on shared/network storage and multiple local processes
leads.detail: DuckDB docs caution about multi-process/write and shared/network paths [S3]. A single-writer project lock and local-filesystem-first scope are proposed, but stale lock recovery and crash races are not implemented.
leads.next_step: Fault-inject lock acquisition, owner death, interrupted journal append, temp output rename, and simultaneous read-only opens on each supported local filesystem.

leads.title: Optional opportunity: shared multi-writer catalog
leads.detail: Real-time collaboration and hosted catalog are outside the brief minimum; the supplied DuckDB concurrency documentation distinguishes current embedded behavior from newer multi-writer options [S3].
leads.next_step: Revisit only if multiple concurrent writers become a user requirement; evaluate the engine/catalog release and operational dependencies at that time.
